subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider-family fallback contract for text agent models, and which shape should own it: wildcard/auto refs, ordered fallbackFamilies, catalog-derived fallbacks, or no new core config?
rationale: This is a public provider/model config contract with auth, quota, cost, and upgrade implications; the code change is straightforward only after maintainers choose the permanent semantics.

options.title: Choose One Core Contract First
options.body: Select the canonical syntax and ordering semantics, then implement only that path with schema, runtime, docs, and compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Fallbacks Only
options.body: Decline new wildcard/grouped config for now and keep provider-family behavior expressed through explicit fallbacks and auth.order.

options.title: Scope to Plugin or Router Work
options.body: Route dynamic model routing to plugin hooks or a separate router proposal, leaving this issue for static fallback-list improvements only if needed.

recommendation.title: Choose One Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Select the canonical syntax and ordering semantics, then implement only that path with schema, runtime, docs, and compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest history across the model fallback core and related product-scope routing decisions.
